'''Isaiah Reese''' (born December 13, 1996) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[BC Uralmash Yekaterinburg|Uralmash]] of the [[VTB United League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Canisius Golden Griffins men's basketball|Canisius College]].

==Early life and high school==
Reese attended [[Miami Christian School]] where he played basketball. He served as a team captain and earned All-Dade County First-Team honors as a senior and was named the Junior Orange Bowl Tournament MVP.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gotham |first1=Paul |title=Canisius adds three to 2016-17 roster - Pickin' Splinters |url=https://pickinsplinters.com/2016/06/29/canisius-adds-three-to-2016-17-roster/ |website=pickinsplinters.com |access-date=12 November 2025 |date=29 June 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
On June 29, 2016, Reese committed to [[Canisius College]] for the 2016–2017 school year under Coach [[Reggie Witherspoon (basketball)|Reggie Witherspoon]]. Reese was one of the first players to join the [[Canisius Golden Griffins men's basketball|Canisius]] program since Witherspoon took over as the program's head new coach. He came to Canisius after spending the 2015–2016 academic year at [[DME Academy]] in [[Daytona Beach, Florida]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball Adds Three to 2016-17 Roster |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2016/6/29/211043798.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=29 June 2016}}</ref>

On December 12, 2016, Reese was named the [[Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference|MAAC]] Rookie of the Week after he averaged 16.5 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 3 assists per game in a pair of non-league games. He was the first Canisius freshman to earn the conference's rookie of the week award since the 2014–2015 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Reese Named MAAC Rookie of the Week |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2016/12/12/211354435.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=12 December 2016}}</ref> On December 27, 2016, Reese was named the MAAC Rookie of the Week again. This was the second time in the last three weeks where he was honored as the conference's top rookie performer. He was the second MAAC freshman that year to earn the league's rookie of the week honors twice.<ref>{{cite web |title=Reese Earns MAAC Rookie of the Week Honors |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2016/12/27/211377295.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=27 December 2016}}</ref>

On November 20, 2017, Reese was named MAAC Player of the Week. He averaged 18.5 points, 7.5 rebounds, 7.5 assists and 2 steals per game in non-league games against [[United States Air Force Academy]] and [[Youngstown State University]]. He was the first [[NCAA Division I]] player to record a [[triple-double]] that season and he was the first MAAC player to reach the feat since [[Scott Machado]] from Iona had a triple-double at [[Marist University]] on February 12, 2012.<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Reese Named MAAC Player of the Week |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2017/11/20/mens-basketball-isaiah-reese-named-maac-player-of-the-week.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=20 November 2017}}</ref> On January 22, 2018, Reese was named the MAAC's Player of the Week after he averaged 21.5 points, 5 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 4.5 steals in road victories against [[Manhattan College]] and [[Iona University]]. This was the second time that season that Reese earned the league's player of the week honors.<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Reese Named MAAC Player of the Week |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2018/1/22/mens-basketball-isaiah-reese-named-maac-player-of-the-week.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=22 January 2018}}</ref> On February 26, 2018, Reese was again named MAAC Player of the Week after the team beat [[Niagara University]] and Marist to secure a share of the 2017-2018 MAAC regular-season championship. This was the third time that season that he was honored as the MAAC Player of the Week. He avereaged 21.5 points per game, 3.5 rebounds, 6.5 assists and 2 steals per game. He was also named to the All-MAAC First Time, making him the first Canisius guard to have that honor since [[Billy Baron]] in 2013–2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Reese and Molson Earn MAAC Weekly Awards |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2018/2/26/mens-basketball-reese-and-molson-earn-maac-weekly-awards.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=26 February 2018}}</ref>

On March 15, 2018, Reese was named to the 2017-2018 [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] Division I All-District Second Team. He was the first Golden Griffin to earn NABC All-District honors since [[Billy Baron]] was recognized after the 2013–2014 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Crumpton and Reese Earn All-District Honors |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2018/3/15/mens-basketball-crumpton-and-reese-earn-all-district-honors.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=15 March 2018}}</ref>

On April 11, 2018, Reese placed his name into consideration for the [[2018 NBA Draft]], but added that he would not sign with an agent to preserve his college eligibility. He became the first Canisius sophomore since 1994 to earn All-MAAC First Team honors after he averaged 16.9 points, 5.8 rebounds, 4.7 assists, and 2.2 steals per game during the 2017–2018 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Reese Declares for 2018 NBA Draft |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2018/4/11/baseball-isaiah-reese-declares-for-2018-nba-draft.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=11 April 2018}}</ref> On May 29, 2018, he withdrew his name from consideration for the [[2018 NBA Draft]]. During that time, he participated in pre-draft workouts with the [[Boston Celtics]], [[Denver Nuggets]], and the [[Houston Rockets]]. He would retain his seasons of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Reese Withdraws Name from NBA Draft |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2018/5/29/mens-basketball-isaiah-reese-withdraws-name-from-nba-draft.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=29 May 2018}}</ref>

On June 20, 2018, Reese was named the Canisius College Most Improved Player for the 2017–2018 season. He became the first Canisius player in program's history to record a triple-double when he posted 23 points, 11 rebounds, and 11 assists in the team's win over [[Youngstown State University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Men’s Basketball Announces 2017-18 Team Awards |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2018/6/20/mens-basketball-announces-2017-18-team-awards.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=20 June 2018}}</ref>

On October 23, 2018, Reese was named the 2018-2019 MAAC Preseason Player of the Year. He joined former Canisius guard, [[Billy Baron]], as the only two players in program history to be named the MAAC Preseason Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Reese Named MAAC Preseason POY, Molson Earns Second-Team Honors |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2018/10/23/mens-basketball-reese-named-maac-preseason-poy-molson-earns-second-team-honors.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=23 October 2018}}</ref>

On November 27, 2018, Reese was one of 50 mid-major players named to the 2018-2019 [[Lou Henson]] Award Watch List. He is the only player from MAAC school to make that year's watch list and one of 13 juniors to be recognized.<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Reese Named to Lou Henson Award Watch List |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2018/11/27/mens-basketball-isaiah-reese-named-to-lou-henson-award-watch-list.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=27 November 2018}}</ref>

On January 21, 2019, Reese was named the MAAC Player of the Week. This was the first time that season a Canisius player has been recognized. In two games, he averaged 13 points, 8 assists, 6.5 rebounds, and 2.5 blocked shots.<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Reese Named MAAC Player of the Week |url=https://gogriffs.com/news/2019/1/21/mens-basketball-isaiah-reese-named-maac-player-of-the-week.aspx |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=21 January 2019}}</ref>

In April 2019, Reese filed as an early entry candidate for the [[2019 NBA Draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NBA announces early entry candidates for 2019 NBA Draft {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2019-draft-early-entry-candidates-official-release |website=NBA |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA Draft]], Reese joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2019 NBA Summer League Rosters |url=https://www.hoopshype.com/story/sports/nba/2019/06/27/nba-summer-league-rosters-2019/82919592007/ |website=HoopsHype |access-date=12 November 2025}}</ref> In the 2019 [[NBA G League]] Draft, Reese was picked in the First Round as the Sixth pick by the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chick |first1=John |title=Former 2nd overall pick Thabeet taken in G League draft |url=https://www.thescore.com/nba/news/1863487 |website=theScore.com |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=26 October 2019}}</ref>

===Santa Cruz Warriors (2019–2021)===
On January 12, 2021, the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] announced their roster for the 2020-2021 [[NBA G League]] season that would take place at the [[ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex]] in [[Orlando, Florida]] and it consisted of four returning rights players including Reese.<ref>{{cite web |title=SANTA CRUZ WARRIORS ANNOUNCE 2020-21 ROSTER |url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2020-21-roster |website=Santa Cruz Warriors |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

In October 2021, the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] traded the returning player rights of Reese to the [[College Park Skyhawks]] for the 30th overall pick Kalob Ledoux.<ref>{{cite web |title=Warriors Complete Trade To Acquire Eighteenth Overall Pick Isaiah Ross In Three-Team Trade |url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/warriors-complete-trade-to-acquire-eighteenth-overall-pick-isaiah-ross-in-three-team-trade |website=Santa Cruz Warriors |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

===Guelph Nighthawks (2021)===
In March 2021, Reese joined the [[Guelph Nighthawks]] after two seasons in the NBA G League.<ref>{{cite web |title=Guelph Nighthawks Sign Former Santa Cruz Warriors Guard, Isaiah Reese |url=https://www.cebl.ca/news/guelph-nighthawks-sign-guard-isaiah-reese |website=www.cebl.ca |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref> On June 10, 2021, the [[Guelph Nighthawks]] announced their training camp roster which consisted of Reese.<ref>{{cite web |title=Guelph Nighthawks release training camp roster |url=https://www.guelphtoday.com/local-sports/guelph-nighthawks-release-training-camp-roster-3865016 |website=GuelphToday.com |language=en |date=10 June 2021}}</ref>

===London Lions (2021–2022)===
In July 2021, Reese signed with the [[London Lions]] and joined [[Kylor Kelley]] and [[Julian Washburn]] as other Americans on the team.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kylor Kelley confirmed to join London Lions for upcoming season |url=https://www.talkbasket.net/130948-kylor-kelley-confirmed-to-join-london-lions-for-upcoming-season |website=TalkBasket.net |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en |date=21 July 2021}}</ref> At the end of the 2021–2022 season, Reese was named the [[British Basketball League]] First Team and Forward of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |title=BBL Championship Basketball 2021-2022, News, Teams, Scores, Stats, Standings, Awards - eurobasket |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/United-Kingdom/British-Basketball-League_2021-2022.aspx |website=www.eurobasket.com |access-date=12 November 2025}}</ref>

===Parma Pari Perm (2022–2024)===
On March 29, 2023, Reese was the MVP of the [[VTB United League]] after averaging 16.8 points, 8.4 rebounds, 7.2 assists and 2.4 steals. He even set his new season-high with 26 points.<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Reese is the MVP of March {{!}} VTB United League - Official Website |url=https://vtb-league.com/en/news/isaiah-reese-is-the-mvp-of-march/ |website=vtb-league.com |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2024, Reese was part of the 2024 [[VTB United League]] All Star Game. He was a starter for Team Pascual alongside [[Jeremiah Martin]], Anton Astapkovich, [[Jalen Reynolds]] and [[Octavius Ellis]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The All-Star Game 2024 Starting Lineups {{!}} VTB United League - Official Website |url=https://vtb-league.com/en/news/the-all-star-game-2024-starting-lineups/ |website=vtb-league.com |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

===Yukatel Merkezefendi Belediyesi Basket Denizli (2024)===
On July 23, 2024, Reese signed with [[Merkezefendi Belediyesi Denizli Basket]] for the 2024–2025 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Merkezefendi signs Isaiah Reese |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/883336/Merkezefendi-signs-Isaiah-Reese |website=www.eurobasket.com |access-date=12 November 2025}}</ref>

===ASP Promitheas Patras (2024–2025)===
On November 29, 2024, Reese signed with [[Promitheas Patras B.C.]] after starting the season with [[Merkezefendi Belediyesi Denizli Basket]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Reese (ex Merkezefendi) agreed terms with Promitheas |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Basketball%20Champions%20League/news/904328/Isaiah-Reese-(ex-Merkezefendi)-agreed-terms-with-Promitheas |website=eurobasket.com |access-date=12 November 2025}}</ref> On June 10, 2025, following the 2024–2025 season, Reese was named to the [[Greek Basketball League]] Second Team alongside [[Nikola Milutinov]], [[Hunter Hale]], Jordon Varnado, and [[Juancho Hernangomez]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Eurobasket.com All-Greek GBL Awards 2025 |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/937294/Eurobasket.com-All-Greek-GBL-Awards-2025 |website=www.eurobasket.com |access-date=12 November 2025}}</ref>

===Hsinchu Toplus Lioneers (2025)===
On August 20, 2025, Reese signed with the [[Hsinchu Toplus Lioneers]] of the [[Taiwan Professional Basketball League]] (TPBL).<ref>{{cite news |title=曾在NBA發展聯盟砍34分 攻城獅新洋將力獅加盟 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/3018808 |accessdate=August 20, 2025 |work=ETtoday |date=August 20, 2025 }}</ref> On November 24, the [[Hsinchu Toplus Lioneers]] terminated the contract relationship with Reese.<ref>{{cite news |title=1場未打轉戰俄羅斯聯賽 攻城獅宣布與力獅解約 |url=https://sports.ltn.com.tw/news/breakingnews/5256060 |accessdate=November 24, 2025 |work=Liberty Times Net |date=November 24, 2025 }}</ref>

===Uralmash Yekaterinburg (2025–present)===
On November 22, 2025, Reese signed with the [[BC Uralmash Yekaterinburg|Uralmash]] of the [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Айзея Риз — новый игрок БК «Уралмаш»! |url=https://bcuralmash.ru/news/ajzeya-riz-novyj-igrok-bk-uralmash/ |date=November 22, 2025 |website=БК Уралмаш |access-date=November 23, 2025 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Reese is the son of Kenneth Reese and Frances Eberhardt. He has two younger brothers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Isaiah Reese - Men's Basketball |url=https://gogriffs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/isaiah-reese/5177 |website=Canisius University Athletics |access-date=12 November 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
